context: a single passage from a letter by William Kemp, which you are answering on its own
exchanges: I have received your very kind letter of the 1 Inst. and I feel deeply grateful for the manner in which you express your sentiments towards me.— I trust my character is not otherwise than what you suppose, I would sooner have my right hand to fail, than put it forth to place one spurious pebble (knowing it to be such) upon that splended structure which is being raised by such Master minds. I am only sorrie upon your account, as you have taken so much interest, and trouble in the matter, As for my part, it matters nothing, the investigation has given a pleasure that amply repays any trouble in the concern.—
Allow me to express my respect at the pleasant tone of your last letter, after what would have been to me, in your case a considerable mortification.
